sources.title: HarmonyOS network dependency discovery and fallback contract approved in task context
claims: Use the Drill UGC api layer as a design reference without assuming its project-specific libraries exist.
Before network implementation, determine whether the supplied dependency is valid and whether the requested tool symbol can be resolved.
When the supplied tool is unavailable, search the current project for an established network-request tool.
When no suitable project tool exists, create the minimum required network implementation while preserving reusable responsibility and directory abstractions.
Apply the rule through the HarmonyOS development workflow and existing Skill rather than creating a task-specific Skill.
Commit and push the Domain, synchronize Harness and Domain, update the CLI repository, and update the local CLI installation.

sources.title: Drill HarmonyOS UGC network layer and common_app transport
claims: The UGC module separates endpoint constants, a repository interface, repository implementation, service orchestration, request and response models, and ViewModel consumption.
The UGC module declares common_app as a local dependency and imports its exported httpCall, BaseApi, response helpers, logging, and base response types.
common_app selects an ICall implementation backed by the project SDK's RemoteCommunicationKit and project-specific interceptors, authentication, routing, toast, URL, and logging behavior.

The example's responsibility split is reusable, while its package names, tool symbols, response envelope, authentication, routing, user messaging, URLs, singleton assembly, and implementation details are project-specific.
Some observed non-success branches in the exemplar neither resolve nor reject the created Promise, so the exemplar cannot be copied as a correctness template.
